stories.title: How Britain’s railways are struggling in the heat – and can they be fixed?
stories.summary: Problems including derailments have hit network during one of the hottest and driest summers on record Britain’s railways have faced a string of heat-related problems this summer, including a derailment near Lewes in East Sussex two weeks ago that injured 30 people, and another the next day when the rear carriages of a Greater Anglia train derailed “in an upright position” at Wickford railway station in Essex , with no reported injuries. The problems came during one of the hottest and driest summers on record, with a series of heatwaves, and drought declared across large parts of England and Wales. Britain’s railways, built for a cooler, wetter climate, have been put under pressure. Network

stories.title: US Federal Reserve’s Kevin Warsh gears up for key Jackson Hole conference as inflation fears mount – business live
stories.summary: Rolling coverage of the latest events in global financial markets, the economy and major corporate moves In the metals market, supply fears have pushed the zinc price up to a four-year high. body: Zinc, which is used to galvanise steel, hit $3,955 a metric tonne this morning, its highest since May 2022.
LME [zinc] inventories have been drawn sharply lower, mine and smelter disruptions have restricted refined availability, and supply outside China has become notably tight.
With consumers facing a thinner pool of immediately available units, relatively modest buying has produced a larger price response than elsewhere in the complex.
Copper remains supported by the same availability concerns.
